summary: Presents a framework to help writers of certificate policies and certification practice statements for public key infrastructures. It provides a comprehensive list of topics that might need covering. It obsoletes RFC 2527 and is informational.

eli5.summary: A group that hands out digital ID cards needs a rule book explaining how careful it is. This gives writers a checklist of topics so they do not forget something important.

questions: what is a certification practice statement
subtitle: A checklist of topics for writing the rule book of a certification authority.

tldr.problem: Relying on a certificate depends on how the issuing authority works: how it checks identities, protects keys and limits its liability. Each PKI wrote its policy documents differently, so they were hard to compare.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC explains certificate policies (CP) and certification practice statements (CPS), and gives a framework of nine primary components, expanded into detailed topics, that a writer can cover or mark as no stipulation.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational framework, not a standard and not a specific policy. It obsoletes RFC 2527 with a reorganized structure designed to be easier for lawyers to review.

today: RFC 3647 is an Informational framework that obsoletes RFC 2527. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope of the Framework
sections.content:
A certificate binds a public key to information about its subject. A relying party uses that binding, for example to check a signature or send encrypted email. How far the relying party can trust it depends on the practices of the certification authority (CA), its security controls, the subscriber's responsibilities, and the CA's stated liability terms.

The document has two purposes. It explains what a certificate policy and a certification practice statement are, how they differ, and how they relate to subscriber and relying party agreements. It also gives writers a framework of elements to consider. It does not define a particular CP or CPS, and it does not give legal advice.

The framework mostly assumes X.509 version 3 certificates, but is meant to be adaptable to other certificate formats. The RFC calls it a flexible tool, not a rigid formula.
sections.eli5: When you show an ID card, whether you believe it depends on who made it and how careful they were. This memo helps those card makers write down how careful they are.

sections.title: Certificate Policies and Practice Statements
sections.content:
An X.509 certificate policy (CP) is a named set of rules that indicates the applicability of a certificate to a particular community or class of application with common security requirements. A CP is identified in a certificate by an Object Identifier (OID). The RFC's example is a policy set with different assurance levels, where the Government of Canada PKI Policy Management Authority defines eight policies with levels from rudimentary to high.

A certification practice statement (CPS) states the practices a CA uses in issuing certificates, and also covers management, revocation, renewal and re-keying. A CA may publish a CPS Summary instead of the full document, leaving out sensitive details.

The two differ in focus. A CP says what participants must do and tends to cover multiple CAs, helping them interoperate. A CPS says how one CA meets those requirements and is generally more detailed. One CA with a single CPS can support several CPs, and several CAs with different CPSs can support the same CP.

Neither document automatically binds anyone as a contract. They bind only when a subscriber agreement or relying party agreement incorporates them by reference, or when a document is both a CPS and such an agreement. A PKI Disclosure Statement (PDS) is a short supplement that highlights critical information.
sections.eli5: The policy is the list of rules everyone must follow. The practice statement is one company saying exactly how it follows those rules.

sections.title: How Policies Appear in X.509 Certificates
sections.content:
Three X.509 version 3 extensions support policies. The Certificate Policies extension lists the CPs the CA declares applicable. When a certification path is processed, a CP acceptable to the relying party must appear in every certificate in the path. If the extension is flagged critical, the certificate may be used only in line with at least one listed CP, which the RFC says is meant to protect the CA against claims from a relying party who used a certificate inappropriately.

The Policy Mappings extension may only be used in CA-certificates. It lets a CA say that a policy in its own domain is equivalent to a policy in the subject CA's domain, so two organizations can cross-certify without reissuing every certificate. The Policy Constraints extension can require explicit policy indications in later certificates, and can disable policy mapping, which helps control transitive trust.

Each policy can also carry policy qualifiers. RFC 3280 defines two: a CPS Pointer, which is a URI pointing to a CPS, CPS Summary, relying party agreement or PDS, and a User Notice, which is text shown before the certificate is used.
sections.eli5: A digital ID card can carry a little label saying which rule book applies to it. Other labels can say that two companies' rule books count as equal, or that only certain rule books are allowed.

sections.title: The Nine Components of a Set of Provisions
sections.content:
The framework organizes a CP or CPS as a set of provisions, a collection of policy or practice statements spanning standard topics. It has nine primary components: Introduction; Publication and Repository; Identification and Authentication; Certificate Life-Cycle Operational Requirements; Facilities, Management, and Operational Controls; Technical Security Controls; Certificate, CRL, and OCSP Profile; Compliance audit; and Other Business and Legal Matters.

Section 4 expands these into detailed subcomponents. Examples are naming and initial identity validation, certificate application, issuance, renewal, re-key and revocation, key escrow and recovery, physical and personnel controls, audit logging, key pair generation and private key protection, and, under business and legal matters, fees, warranties, liability limits and governing law.

No document has to address every topic. A CP or CPS may state "no stipulation" for any component or element, and drafters may add further levels of subcomponents. The same nine-part structure can also be used to write subscriber agreements, relying party agreements and other PKI-related agreements.
sections.eli5: The checklist has nine big chapters, such as how to prove who you are, how to keep keys safe, and what happens if something goes wrong. You can skip a chapter by writing that it has no rules.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC's security section restates that the trust a relying party can place in a certificate depends on the CA's practices, controls and stated liability terms. The framework addresses technical, procedural, personnel and physical security of CAs, Registration Authorities, repositories, subscribers and relying party cryptographic modules, so that certificate generation, publication, renewal, re-key, usage and revocation happen securely. It singles out the identification and authentication, life-cycle, facility, technical-control, profile and audit components as the ones oriented towards secure operation of PKI entities.
sections.eli5: A good rule book makes sure the people, buildings and computers that make ID cards are all kept safe.

sections.title: Comparison to RFC 2527
sections.content:
This framework is an incremental improvement over RFC 2527, using experience gained deploying CP and CPS documents and coordination with the American Bar Association Information Security Committee. Technically the changes are described as minimal and incremental. Sections 3 to 7 were largely preserved with modest reorganization and new topics.

The new framework gives the certificate life-cycle a full treatment and adds key escrow, key encapsulation and key recovery, and OCSP. Audit now has its own component, repository matters are separate, and business and legal matters move into a new section ordered like a technology licensing agreement. That section also adds topics such as privacy of personal information, liability terms and duration of the document's effectiveness. The aim is to make legal review of CP and CPS documents more efficient.
sections.eli5: This is a tidied-up second edition of an older checklist, rearranged so that lawyers can read it more easily and with a few new topics added.
